title: Atomic Theory and Structure - Chemistry - Subatomic Particles
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which subatomic particle has a charge of zero and a mass of approximately 1 amu?
questions.explain: Neutrons are neutral particles (charge of 0) located in the nucleus and have a mass of approximately 1 atomic mass unit (amu).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Where are electrons located in the modern model of the atom?
options: Inside the nucleus with the protons
Inside the nucleus with the neutrons
In a cloud or region of space surrounding the nucleus
Embedded on the surface of the nucleus
questions.explain: Electrons orbit the nucleus in a diffuse cloud or specific orbitals, occupying the vast majority of the atom's volume but very little of its mass.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which statement correctly compares the relative masses of protons and electrons?
options: A proton has approximately the same mass as an electron.
A proton is approximately 1800 times more massive than an electron.
An electron is approximately 1800 times more massive than a proton.
Protons have mass, while electrons have absolutely zero mass.
questions.explain: Protons and neutrons have a mass of ~1 amu, while electrons have a mass of ~1/1836 amu. Therefore, a proton is roughly 1800 times heavier than an electron.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: In the Rutherford gold foil experiment, what caused the deflection of the small percentage of alpha particles?
options: Repulsion by the dense, positively charged nucleus
questions.explain: Alpha particles are positively charged. When they approached the small, dense, positively charged nucleus of the gold atoms, the strong electrostatic repulsion caused them to deflect.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which subatomic particle identifies an atom as a specific element?
questions.explain: The number of protons (atomic number) defines the identity of an element. Changing the number of protons changes the element.
questions.subject: Chemistry
